A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PA-Tool research. Their complete 25-page documents, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on MetaTool, RoTBench, API-Bank and τ-Bench, together with error analysis, fine-tuning experiments and hyperparameter studies.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional component ablations, human evaluation, schema-transfer tests and noise-robustness results.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains candidate sampling, edit-distance peakedness, maximum-peakedness selection, greedy-reference tie-breaking and collision resolution. New ablation and transfer experiments test variants without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates RoTBench exclusively under Clean conditions; v3 Appendix I adds Slight, Medium, Heavy and Union noise scenarios. Section 6.7 also introduces human understandability and functionality-match evaluation of 199 tools. MetaTool, API-Bank and τ-Bench Retail coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The established main and external baseline approaches remain intact. v3 Table 2 adds tool-only and parameter-only alignment controls against full PA-Tool, providing limited new method comparisons within the component ablation.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include randomized, blinded name comparisons by three annotators, 1–5 ratings and preferences, component controls, and source-target model transfer tests. v3 also adds Qwen3-1.7B/4B thinking-mode configurations and Qwen2.5 fine-tuning experiments. Existing MetaTool splits and default schema-generation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds tool-versus-parameter ablations (Table 2), human clarity case studies (Table 6), cross-model transfer analysis (Table 18) and noise sensitivity tests (Table 19). These examine component contributions and deployment boundaries absent from v2. Existing error analysis, peakedness validation and hyperparameter sweeps are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces paired t-test reporting for human ratings, reporting p < 10^-35 in Section 6.7. This is a localized addition to statistical inference. Both versions already report mean τ-Bench performance over five independent runs; no increase in that run count is stated.

E6.justification: Many RoTBench scores and rankings are revised. In Table 1, Qwen2.5-3B single-turn tool-selection accuracy for Base/PA-Tool changes from 1.9/6.7 to 12.4/18.1; GPT-4.1-mini multi-turn tool selection changes from 28.6 to 71.4. Numerous new study results also appear. The PDFs do not explain all revisions, so these are updated reports rather than established same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), including the similarity threshold, peakedness definition and selection rules, are unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly excludes j = i in v3, matching the exclusion already present in v2 Equation (2). No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 narrows the abstract and contribution statement from approaching state-of-the-art or closed-source performance to improving SLM tool-use accuracy. The introduction also revises the reported RoTBench multi-turn gain to up to 6%. The central training-free schema-adaptation contribution and headline 17% improvement and 80% error-reduction claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 replaces broad superiority claims over EasyTool with model-dependent complementarity and softens the SFT degradation interpretation from catastrophic forgetting to suggested reduced generalization. It adds interpretations of readability, schema transfer and noise sensitivity, plus naming-bias and human-clarity risks. The warning about generation overhead for very large tool libraries is removed.

D1.justification: The promised future code release becomes a stated available repository link. v3 newly specifies two preceding interactions followed by third-turn RoTBench evaluation, without establishing a between-version procedure change. The reported SFT GPU changes from A6000 48GB to A100 80GB; core hyperparameters, prompts and software-stack information remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds PLAY2PROMPT in the discussion of future description refinement and removes references to Self-Refine, BacktrackAgent and SWEET-RL. The central positioning around schema alignment and contamination-detection peakedness remains. Publication-metadata updates and consolidation of the duplicate API-Bank reference do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, results interpretations and several appendix explanations are extensively rewritten. Section 6 reorganizes existing analyses around mechanism, compatibility and generalization. Algorithm, example, collision and hyperparameter material is consolidated into Appendix A, while prompt templates are collected in Appendix L.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn with weather-tool examples and clearer schema/component displays. v3 adds several analysis tables and groups the expanded model table by model type. v2 Figures 12–14 are removed, while the hyperparameter plot is relocated as Figure 5. Tables and prompt panels are substantially rearranged throughout the appendices.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects overgeneralizations about EasyTool and SFT and adds controlled evidence on component contributions, human readability, transfer and noise robustness that v2 lacked. Access documentation and organization also improve. However, extensive RoTBench score revisions remain unexplained, and Appendix E's narrowed error taxonomy conflicts with the retained classification prompt in Figure 11. These unresolved issues limit the overall quality gain.
